tasks.short: Watch the traffic flow to locate safe gaps, then signal pedestrians when they can cross.

steps.what: Crossing guard monitors traffic flow to locate safe gaps for pedestrians
Crossing guard signals pedestrians when they can cross the street

tasks.design: Nothing changes. Judging a safe gap in moving traffic is a split-second call made on the spot; no software decides when children cross.
tasks.previous_blocker: None; the task is watching and judging traffic.
tasks.still_hard: Drivers who speed or do not stop.
tasks.human_edge: Reading a driver's intent from how the car slows down.

evidence.claim: Judging gaps in traffic for pedestrians is done in real time by the guard; no software makes this call.

assumptions: Boundary: from waiting pedestrians to pedestrians crossed; road design is outside.
Input contract: none; the guard watches the street.
No new work: nothing changes in this task, so the added effort is zero.
research_questions: None for software; road design questions belong to the municipality.

incremental.description: No added work for the crossing guard; nothing changes in this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low and high: the task stays fully with the guard.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Tell students and adults the crossing rules at the crossing, and hand out flyers on the rules at the start of the school year.

steps.what: Crossing guard communicates traffic and crossing rules to students and adults
Crossing guard hands out flyers on crossing rules to parents

tasks.design: The school sends the crossing rules to parents through its parent app ({CHAT}) at the start of the year, so the guard hands out fewer paper flyers. Explaining the rules at the crossing stays with the guard.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rules reached parents only on paper at the crossing.
tasks.enabler_now: Schools reach parents through parent apps.
tasks.still_hard: Parents who drive past do not read the message.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a hurried parent to wait for the signal in front of their child.

reach.learn: Whether parents follow the crossing rules better.

evidence.claim: Schools can send messages to parents through parent apps.

assumptions: Boundary: from people at the crossing to flyers handed out; school traffic policy is outside.
Input contract: the school office sends the message; fallback is paper flyers.
Explaining at the crossing does not change.
Parents read the message as they would a flyer; no added parent time.
research_questions: Do parents follow the crossing rules better?

incremental.description: Crossing guard gives the school the rules text each year.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few flyers today; high: a school with many new parents each year.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set up signs and lanterns, then direct traffic and warn of hazards with signs, flags and hand signals.

steps.what: Crossing guard sets up and removes signs and lanterns
Crossing guard directs traffic movement and warns of hazards using signs, flags and hand signals

tasks.design: Nothing changes. Directing traffic with signs, flags and hand signals is physical work on the street; the guard decides each movement.
tasks.previous_blocker: None; the task is physical and on the spot.
tasks.human_edge: Making eye contact with a driver before stepping out.

evidence.claim: Directing traffic with signs and hand signals is physical work; no software applies.

assumptions: Boundary: from the shift start to traffic directed; traffic plans are outside.
Input contract: none; signs and lanterns are on site.
No new work: nothing changes in this task, so the added effort is zero.

incremental.description: No added work for the crossing guard; nothing changes in this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low and high: the task stays fully with the guard.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe unsafe behavior of children, decide what to report and note it, send the note to the school office, and talk with school officials about serious cases.

steps.what: Crossing guard observes unsafe behavior of children at the crossing
Crossing guard decides what to report and notes what happened
Crossing guard drops the note at the school office to report to school officials
Crossing guard talks with school officials about serious cases

tasks.design: A short report form on the guard's phone ({OTHER}) with date, place and what happened replaces handwritten notes; once the guard has written and checked it, it goes to the school office's mailbox. Children are described by what they did; names only when the guard knows them. Serious cases are still discussed by phone or in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were handwritten and walked to the school office.
tasks.enabler_now: Simple phone forms can send reports to a mailbox.
tasks.still_hard: The guard often does not know the child's name or school.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a reckless habit apart from a one-off mistake.

reach.task: Talk with pupils and parents about road safety
reach.learn: Whether reports arrive the same day.

evidence.claim: Simple phone forms can send structured reports to a mailbox.
Reports about named children are personal data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from children at the crossing to the case discussed; school follow-up is outside.
Input contract: the school office reads its mailbox daily; fallback is paper notes.
Observing and talking with officials do not change.
School officials' time does not change.
research_questions: Do reports reach the school the same day more often?

incremental.description: Crossing guard learns to use the phone form.

approvals.approved_version: The incident note as written and checked by the guard in s2.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a school close to the crossing; high: a school office a walk away.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The crossing guard keeps watching traffic, directing it and keeping children safe; paper flyers and walked notes shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A guard whose full attention stays on the street.
